# Organs
Trauma to the chest and head can damage the organs inside. Each organ has its own health and goes through five stages as it's damaged: [color=#3cff6b]healthy[/color], [color=#ffc300]bruised[/color], [color=#ff8a3d]damaged[/color], [color=#ff3b30]failing[/color] and dead.
A health analyzer shows organ damage to trained medics.
## Recovery - A healthy or bruised organ slowly heals on its own, but only up to 90% of its health (85% for the brain). - A damaged, failing or dead organ won't recover by itself. It needs organ repair drugs or surgery.
## The Organs ### Heart - [bold]Bruised[/bold]: the heart races (tachycardia). - [bold]Damaged or failing[/bold]: the heartbeat becomes irregular (arrhythmia), the patient slowly suffocates and takes toxin damage. A failing heart also bleeds internally. - If the pulse drops too low for too long, the heart stops: [bold]cardiac arrest[/bold]. The patient can't get oxygen and collapses within seconds. - A defibrillator can't restart a heart that's failing or dead. Repair it first.
### Lungs - Damaged lungs can't take in enough air, so the patient suffocates. - [bold]Pulmonary edema[/bold]: the lungs flood and breathing becomes laboured. Through a stethoscope the lungs sound wet. - Badly damaged lungs make the patient cough up blood, and failing lungs bleed internally. - Breathing from an oxygen tank through internals (a mask connected to the tank) clears suffocation damage three times as fast as normal breathing.
### Liver - [bold]Hepatic failure[/bold]: a damaged liver stops clearing toxins from the blood.
### Kidneys - [bold]Renal failure[/bold]: damaged kidneys stop filtering the blood, so chemicals linger in the body longer.
### Stomach - A damaged stomach causes nausea and vomiting.
### Brain - Head trauma can cause a [bold]concussion[/bold], [bold]whiplash[/bold] or a [bold]traumatic brain injury[/bold]. A damaged brain causes splitting headaches that leave the patient disoriented.
### Eyes and Ears - Damaged eyes impair vision. - Loud blasts cause tinnitus and can deafen. See [textlink="Hearing Loss" link="CMUGuideHearingLoss"].
## Organ Repair Drugs Each heals its organ a little every cycle while in the bloodstream. All of them overdose at 25u. - [bold]Cardiocaine[/bold]: heart. It also has a small chance each cycle to restart a stopped heart, as long as the heart isn't dead. - [bold]Pulmovine[/bold]: lungs. - [bold]Hepatocytin[/bold]: liver. - [bold]Nephronate[/bold]: kidneys. - [bold]Alkysine[/bold]: brain.
## Organ Surgery - [bold]Suture[/bold] a damaged organ to repair it: the heart, lungs, liver, kidneys or stomach. - [bold]Repair Brain[/bold] and [bold]Repair Eyes[/bold] fix the head's organs. - An organ that's beyond saving can be removed and replaced with a donor organ. A health analyzer shows a missing organ as removed.
See [textlink="Surgery" link="CMUGuideMedicalSurgery"] for how to operate.
